text:
sam: Quick sync — I'm putting together the plan to integrate FlashAttention v2/v3 into the runtime selector. Main goals: safe rollout, clear fallbacks for paged-attn/KV, and telemetry to catch regressions early. Outline coming.

jin: thanks — can you call out the concrete gating metrics we want for canary vs full rollout?

sam: TL;DR proposal: (1) kernel chooser set to `auto` by default; (2) opt-in feature flag for prefer_flashv3; (3) canary at 5% traffic for 24h; (4) telemetry thresholds: p99 latency delta < +5% vs baseline, throughput within -10%, memory < baseline + 200MB, KV hit rate >= 0.7 for prefix heavy workloads. Rollback if any threshold breached or error rate spikes > 0.5%.

pat: 5% sounds right. For throughput we should track tokens/sec and effective batch size distribution. Also track `kv_evictions/sec` and `kv_miss_latency` — we've seen regressions where paged KV causes tail latency.

lee: paging corner: for large sequence lengths (>2048) we should default to paged-attn or fused fallback depending on memory pressure. Need to confirm kernel chooser rule: prefer flashv3 for seq <= 2048 and non-paged KV; otherwise prefer paged kernel. Also add explicit `attn.paged_fallback=true` flag.

sam: putting commands and flags here so ops can test toggles:

```
# internal config API (canary toggle)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  https://config.internal/api/feature-flags \ 
  -d '{"flag":"attn.prefer_flashv3","value":true,"scope":"canary"}'

# kernel chooser override (debug)
redwoodctl node set-runtime-config --kernels.attn=flashv3_override
```

jin: naming for flags? suggest:
- `attn.chooser=auto|flashv2|flashv3|paged|fused`
- `attn.prefer_flashv3=true|false` (scope: per-customer)
- `attn.kv_cache_mode=static|dynamic|paged`
- `attn.paged_fallback=enabled|disabled`

pat: for canary tests I'll run the perf harness against these workloads: conversational (mixed short/long), long-context tokenizer (seq 4096), and embedding-like small seq. Command:

```
perf-harness run --workload conv-mix --duration 30m --traffic 5% --metrics tokens_per_sec,p99_latency,mem_rss,kv_hit_rate
```

lee: note from last run — we observed a ~12% p99 regress for flashv3 on the conv-mix when `kv_cache_mode=dynamic` and cache hit < 0.6. So two mitigations:
1) pin `attn.kv_cache_mode=static` for first canary wave
2) add an automatic fallback when kv_miss_latency > 5ms:
   - if miss latency high -> switch to paged kernel for affected model/version

sam: good catch. I'll add those mitigations to the plan and make static the default for canary. Acceptance criteria now: pass perf harness for 3 workloads at 5% canary for 24h, no p99 > +5% and kv_miss_latency < 5ms. Prepare dashboard and alerts.

ops-bot: canary deploy started: flashv3-canary-group -> 5% traffic, start=1765432120

jin: I'll build the telemetry dashboard: panels for p99, 50/90, tokens/sec, kv_hit_rate, kv_evictions, model_error_rate. I'll add temporary regression alert rules:
- p99 > baseline * 1.05 for 10m
- kv_miss_latency > 5ms for 5m
- token/sec drop > 15% for 15m

pat: running the perf harness now (kicked off at 1765432130). I'll upload raw traces to /perf/flashv3/canary-1765432100.

lee: one more: add a sampling of kernel-level profiles for the canary (nvprof/torchperf) every hour for a subset of requests so we can see kernel choice distribution + memory spikes.

sam: owners
- rollout orchestration + flags: sam
- telemetry + dashboards: jin
- perf harness + canary runs: pat
- KV/paged fallback tests: lee

pat: ack. will post results in this thread after 30m run. :wave:

ops-bot: canary complete: status=PASS, duration=24h simulated (smoke), p99_delta=+2.3%, tokens_sec_change=-4.1%, kv_hit_rate=0.78, kv_miss_latency=3.2ms. Full rollout recommended by owners.

sam: thanks everyone. I'll open a PR for the flag defaults and a rollout playbook and schedule a 1h post-rollout check next week.
